h1: The 6 Best Handheld Steam Cleaners for Grout of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Handheld Grout Steam Cleaners: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 handheld steam cleaners scored on brush quality, tank size and steam pressure for grout lines, led by the DOURARY 18-piece kit.
summary: The DOURARY 1200W kit is the best grout steamer here: a removable 550 ml tank, about 25 minutes per fill, and both steel and nylon brushes. The Gautye adds brass brushes and handle-mounted steam control. The WSRYYCC gives the biggest tank for whole bathrooms. The STMWORLD runs hottest, and the Likzest is the light pick for quick jobs.
intro: Grout cleaning fails for a boring reason: the steam is not the problem, the brush is. Steam softens grime sitting in a porous line, but something still has to scrub it out. A machine with a good jet and a flimsy nylon brush will leave a gray stripe behind, while a modest unit with the right bristles can finish the job.

That shaped how we ranked six handheld steamers. Brush selection and nozzle shape came first, followed by how long a tank lasts across a floor of tile, how the steam is controlled, and the weight you carry while kneeling. One warning applies to all of them: steel brushes can scratch polished stone and glazed tile, so test a hidden corner first.

products.name: DOURARY 1200W Handheld Steam Cleaner, 18-Piece Kit
products.verdict: A removable 550 ml tank, steel and nylon brushes and about 25 minutes per fill.
products.description:
DOURARY packs a 1200W heater, steam around 230°F and a removable 550 ml tank into a kit that includes steel and nylon brushes. It heats in 10 to 12 seconds and runs about 25 minutes on a fill, which is long enough to do a shower floor.

The removable tank is the key practical feature: you can top it off at the sink without hauling the whole machine. It beats the STMWORLD because it runs far longer and ships with more brush options. The two steam levels are coarse next to the six-level units, but grout rarely needs fine adjustment.

Buy it for bathrooms and kitchen backsplashes with stubborn lines. The caveat is that the steel brush belongs on grout only, not on polished tile.
products.idealFor: Bathroom floors and backsplashes with stained lines.
products.skipIf: Your tile is polished stone or easily scratched.

products.name: Gautye Steam Cleaner, 3-Level Handle, 15 Accessories
products.verdict: Three steam levels on the handle plus nylon and brass brushes.
products.description:
Gautye puts three steam levels on the handle, so you adjust without stopping, and supplies nylon and brass brushes among 15 accessories. Steam reaches up to 212°F at up to 3 bar, with a heat-up near 15 seconds.

It ranks second because brass is the sweet spot for grout: harder than nylon, kinder to tile than steel. Next to the DOURARY it gives you better brush material but a lower steam temperature and no stated tank life. Against the WSRYYCC, it trades tank size for handle controls.

Good for mixed surfaces where you switch between delicate tile and stained grout. The caveat is the 212°F maximum, the coolest here, so tough grease may need extra dwell time.
products.idealFor: Mixed tile and grout where brush choice matters.

products.name: WSRYYCC 6-Level Handheld Steam Cleaner, 16 Accessories
products.verdict: A 1.25 L tank with 3 bar pressure and six touch levels for big jobs.
products.description:
The WSRYYCC carries 1.25 L of water, the biggest tank in this ranking, and steams at 221°F and 3 bar through six touch-controlled levels. A 15-second heat-up and 16 accessories make it ready for a whole room.

It places third because its brush selection is not highlighted for grout the way the DOURARY and Gautye are. What it does give you is endurance: a full bathroom of grout lines before a refill. Its six levels also let you reduce steam near sealed or delicate surfaces.

Choose it for a big tiled floor or a commercial-style kitchen. The caveat is the heavier tank, which makes a long kneeling session more tiring.
products.idealFor: Large tiled floors and long cleaning sessions.
products.skipIf: You want a light unit for quick spot jobs.

products.name: STMWORLD 1200W Handheld Steam Cleaner, 10-in-1 Kit
products.verdict: 248°F steam, a grout brush in the kit and a flexible hose for tight spots.
products.description:
STMWORLD reaches 248°F steam from a 1200W heater and includes a grout brush with its flexible hose. A 400 ml tank (13.5 oz) and a 3-minute heat-up complete the spec.

It ranks fourth because heat is its strength and tank size its weakness. Hotter steam loosens soap scum and grease faster, but 400 ml does not stretch across a floor. The flexible hose is a genuine help on shower corners and around fixtures, where rigid wands cannot reach, and it makes the unit a strong spot cleaner.

Buy it for detail work on a backsplash, shower niche or tub edge. The caveat is frequent refills on any large area.
products.idealFor: Backsplashes, shower corners and tub edges.
products.skipIf: You are cleaning a whole floor.

products.name: Suu66 Handheld Steam Cleaner, 500 ml Tank, 19-Piece Kit
products.verdict: A 19-piece kit with a 500 ml tank and a one-click safety lock.
products.description:
Suu66 supplies a 19-piece kit, 230°F steam, a one-click safety lock and a 500 ml tank, with a 350 ml recommended fill. Heat-up takes 3 to 5 minutes and one fill lasts about 10 to 15 minutes.

It ranks fifth because run time is short next to the DOURARY and the listing does not single out grout brushes. The 19 pieces are the most you can get for the money, though, and the safety lock is helpful in a household with kids. Compared with the Likzest below, it has a bigger tank and more accessories.

Pick it for small bathrooms and occasional grout sessions. The caveat is the 350 ml recommended fill, which limits you to short bursts.
products.idealFor: Small bathrooms and occasional grout cleaning.
products.skipIf: You want to finish a large floor in one go.

products.name: Likzest 230°F Pressurized Handheld Steam Cleaner
products.verdict: A 2.6 lb pressurized steamer with 14 accessories and a safety lock.
products.description:
The Likzest is the lightest unit at 2.6 lb, with 230°F pressurized steam, a safety lock, a heat-resistant housing and 14 accessories. The cord is 9.8 ft.

It ranks last because the listing gives no tank size or brush detail, which are what matter for grout. Its low weight does help when you hold it overhead on tile walls. Against the Suu66, it sacrifices accessories for comfort, and the DOURARY outclasses it on brushes and tank life.

Good for quick passes on small bathroom walls and fixtures. The caveat is that missing tank data means you should expect short runs between fills.
products.idealFor: Tile walls and quick fixture touch-ups.
products.skipIf: You want long runs on floor grout.

whatMatters.detail: Grout is porous, so steam alone leaves residue. Nylon brushes are gentle, brass is firmer, and steel is the most aggressive. The DOURARY ships steel and nylon, and the Gautye ships nylon and brass. Check the listing for brush material and test steel on a hidden spot, as it can scratch polished or glazed tile.

Grout cleaning is slow, since you hold the brush on each line. A bigger tank cuts refill breaks. The WSRYYCC carries 1.25 L, the DOURARY 550 ml with a removable design, and the STMWORLD only 400 ml. On a listing, look for milliliters and minutes per fill, not just the word large.

Pressure pushes steam into the grout pores, where grime hides. The WSRYYCC and Gautye list 3 bar. Higher pressure usually helps, but it also throws water on walls. Check for adjustable levels, which the WSRYYCC and Gautye provide, if you clean near wood trim or painted surfaces.

A narrow jet nozzle concentrates steam on a grout line, while a wide head wastes it on tile faces. Look for a pointed nozzle and a flexible hose for corners, as on the STMWORLD. Round brushes work for floors, and small angled brushes reach corners.

Steaming can strip grout sealer, so reseal after deep cleaning. Wipe loosened grime with a microfiber cloth before it dries back into the pores, and let the area dry. If your grout is unsealed, steam it sparingly and plan to apply sealer.

faq.q: Will a steam cleaner remove old grout stains?
faq.a: It helps loosen soil, but dark stains may need a brush and a grout cleaner. The DOURARY's steel brush and the Gautye's brass brush scrub where steam softens. Deep discoloration may need regrouting.
It can strip sealer and, on cracked grout, push water behind tile. Use the Gautye's lower levels near trim and reseal after cleaning. Check that grout is intact before steaming.

faq.q: Is a steel brush worth it over nylon?
faq.a: On grout, yes, since steel scrubs out set grime that nylon cannot. The DOURARY includes both. Keep steel off polished stone, glass and glazed tile, where it leaves scratches.

faq.q: How do I set up for a bathroom floor?
faq.a: Fill the tank with distilled water if possible, let the unit reach full steam, and work in small sections. Keep a microfiber cloth ready to wipe loosened dirt, and refill the WSRYYCC or DOURARY before starting a new row.

faq.q: How often should I descale the unit?
faq.a: Descale when steam weakens or you see white deposits, more often with hard water. Using distilled water in the Suu66 or STMWORLD slows buildup and protects the heater.

faq.q: Can I use it on colored grout?
faq.a: Usually yes, since steam does not bleach. Test a hidden section first. Colored grout that is unsealed can darken when wet, and aggressive steel brushing can wear its surface.

finalTake: The DOURARY 1200W kit is the best handheld steamer for grout because it pairs a removable tank with proper steel and nylon brushes. The Gautye is the pick for mixed surfaces, and the WSRYYCC is the tank-size champion. Choose the STMWORLD for corner detail, and always reseal grout after a deep steam clean.
